The '''2003–04''' season was '''Chelsea F.C.'s''' 12th consecutive season in the [[Premier League]] and 98th year as a club. In July 2003, long-time chairman [[Ken Bates]] sold the club to Russian billionaire [[Roman Abramovich]]. Manager [[Claudio Ranieri]] was sacked on 31 May 2004 and was replaced by [[José Mourinho]] for the following season.

Chelsea finished the season as runners-up in the [[2003–04 FA Premier League|Premier League]]. In the [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] Chelsea reached the semi-finals against [[AS Monaco FC|AS Monaco]], but failed to reach the final, losing 5–3 on aggregate to the French side. They also exited the [[2003–04 FA Cup|FA Cup]] in the fifth round to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and the [[2003–04 Football League Cup|Carling Cup]] in the quarter-finals to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]].

==Team kit==
The team kit was produced by [[Umbro]]. The shirt sponsor was the airline [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]]; the kit bore the "Fly Emirates" logo. Chelsea's home kit was all blue with a white collar. Their new away kit was all white with black and blue stripes down the centre. Last season's away kit (all black with blue accents) was retained as the club's third kit.
